title: Signed coherent shifts and the strict completed scalar comparison
statement: Let l be prime, E and L finite extensions of Q_l, ι:E→L a Q_l-algebra inclusion, and Y any scheme. Let C(P)=Cone(1-s_P)[-1] be the specified product-cocone scalar extension and b_P the canonical quotient-tensor comparison with zero second coordinate [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Fix the product shift isomorphism obtained by the ordinary tensor and restriction shifts at every finite quotient followed by the canonical product-preservation comparison. Then C has a coherent integer shift structure. On the two cocone inclusions it has respectively this product shift and (-1)^m times this product shift, including the standard degree reindexing. Moreover the ordinary tensor shift followed by b_P[m] equals b_(P[m]) followed by this C-shift, for every cochain complex P and every integer m. No K-flatness or completeness assumption is needed.

proof.text: Each finite scalar level is the termwise functor of ordinary extension followed by restriction to the completion. For a module M, evaluate the given transition on the zero-differential constant cochain complex at degree zero to obtain a natural module transition. Its termwise prolongation has the same sheafified tensor formula as the given chain transition; uniqueness identifies them. Every termwise natural transformation commutes with the identity-component cochain shifts. Thus all tower transitions commute with the level shifts. Use the fused termwise functor shift on the native tower levels. Its comparison with the two-factor tensor/restriction shift follows from functor map_id over arbitrary module categories, before coefficient specialization.

proof.text: The native evaluations of the strict tower are these level functors; its native transition equals the given scalar transition by Functor.ofOpSequence. Apply the native Roos shift construction [lem-weil-roos-comm-shift], whose product projection calculation conjugates the transition endomorphism.

proof.text: The named completedScalarChainProductIso is the product of the finite tensor and restriction shift comparisons followed by the canonical product-preservation comparison. At every finite level the fused termwise shift equals that tensor-then-restriction shift by the functor map_id equation. Hence this fixed product comparison equals ProductShift.productShiftIso [lem-weil-product-comm-shift], and commShift_formula gives the exact normalized coordinate formula [lem-weil-roos-comm-shift]. No arbitrary product comparison is needed.

proof.text: A map from the ordinary scalar extension of M is determined by its values on the sheafified tensor generators. Use the model object equation to reduce to the actual change-of-rings sheafification; the sheafification hom extensionality and tensor induction prove this assertion. The prescribed first component of the chain comparison, after the nth product projection, sends s tensor x to its nth residue tensor x. This formula depends only on P^i. Comparing with the zero-differential complex on P^i therefore shows that the whole first component in degree i depends only on that module. Reindexing degrees proves its shift square at each level, and shifted product-projection extensionality gives the first-component product shift square.

proof.text: The second component of the canonical comparison is zero by its specification. The generic native Roos chain_shift theorem [lem-weil-roos-comm-shift] uses the cocone identity decomposition to factor this map through the first inclusion. The preceding first-component product shift equation therefore gives the full chain equation.
